# droidlite

> droidlite is a lightweight Android emulator for low-end PCs. It boots a 720p,
> 2-vCPU, 1.5 GB Android 15 device with no Google Play, no sensors, no camera,
> no audio and about 30 system apps disabled, so you can install and test an APK
> without Android Studio on a 4-core / 8 GB machine.

- Repository: https://github.com/N1XNAC/droidlite
- License: MIT
- Language: Bash (wraps Google's stock emulator + AOSP system image)
- Platforms: Linux x86_64 (primary), macOS, WSL2
- Requires: KVM (`/dev/kvm`), 4 CPU threads, 4 GB free RAM, ~8 GB disk

## What it does

droidlite is a thin CLI over the Android emulator. It changes no binaries; it
removes cost from configuration and the guest image:

- AVD: 720×1280 @ 320 dpi, 2 vCPU, 1536 MB RAM, 2 GB data, no camera, GPS,
  Bluetooth, NFC, fingerprint, SD card or sensors.
- Boot: no boot animation, audio, metrics, passive GPS or snapshots.
- Guest: up to 35 AOSP/Google apps disabled per user (Calendar, Clock, Gallery,
  Email, Music, Browser, Camera, Print, SIM toolkit, NFC, provisioning, …),
  animations off.
- Install: unused ARM/ARM64/i386 QEMU binaries, ANGLE and crash reporter removed
  (863 MB → 679 MB; 247 MB with `--headless`).

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/N1XNAC/droidlite.git
cd droidlite
./droidlite doctor
./droidlite setup
./droidlite start --headless
./droidlite install app-debug.apk
./droidlite run com.example.app
./droidlite shot /tmp/screen.png
./droidlite stop
```

## Commands

`setup`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `install`, `inspect`, `run`, `logcat`,
`shot`, `screen`, `shell`, `push`, `pull`, `trim`, `untrim`, `reset`, `prune`,
`list`, `doctor`.

All commands are non-interactive. `status --json` emits machine-readable state.
The emulator serial is always `emulator-5554`.

## Facts an assistant should know

- AOSP images run x86_64 native code only. ARM-only APKs need `--image gapps`
  (includes NDK translation) or an x86_64 rebuild.
- There is no Play Store / GMS on the default image. GMS is opt-in via
  `--image gapps` and removed only with `trim --no-gms`.
- Android Studio and Gradle see droidlite as a normal ADB device.
- Headless mode is the low-RAM path: `start --headless`, then `shot` or
  `screen` (scrcpy).
- Guest state is disposable: `reset` wipes user data.
